strapping.0: Boot mode select. Usually the BOOT button.
strapping.2: Must be low or floating at boot for download mode.
strapping.5: SDIO timing. Has an internal pull-up at boot.
strapping.12: MTDI selects VDD_SDIO voltage. An external pull-up at boot can set 1.8 V flash and prevent boot.
strapping.15: MTDO controls boot log output. Internally pulled up.

consumed.9: SPI flash (SD_DATA2) - not broken out on most modules
consumed.10: SPI flash (SD_DATA3) - not broken out on most modules

conditional_free.1: UART0 TX. Free only if you give up the serial console.
conditional_free.3: UART0 RX. Free only if you give up the serial console.
conditional_free.16: Consumed by PSRAM on WROVER modules.
conditional_free.17: Consumed by PSRAM on WROVER modules.

pin_notes.34: Input only. No output driver, and NO internal pull-up or pull-down - fit an external resistor.

notes: GPIO34-39 are input-only AND have no internal pull resistors. A button on one of these needs an external pull-up.
ADC2 is unusable while Wi-Fi is active, exactly as on the S3. On the classic part this is worse, because ADC2 covers most of the convenient pins.
GPIO12 (MTDI) is the classic brick: an external pull-up at boot can select 1.8 V flash.
GPIO6-11 are the flash bus and are not broken out on standard modules.
sources: Espressif ESP32 datasheet and technical reference manual (general knowledge)

sources.ref: Espressif ESP32 datasheet and Technical Reference Manual: input-only GPIO34-39, ADC bank map, strapping pins, flash bus GPIO6-11

corroboration.conservative_rationale: A family fallback that over-reserves: the flash bus GPIO6-11 is marked consumed unconditionally, and GPIO16/17 are only conditionally free because WROVER modules use them for PSRAM. Refusing a pin that a bare WROOM would have allowed is the safe direction.
